# DISK/LightGlue references

Generate `testdata/cv/features/disk/disk_lightglue_matches.npy`, the reference
match list for `Features2d_LightGlue_DISK.Regression`. Requires `numpy` and the
Python bindings of the OpenCV build under test (see below). The file holds one
`(queryIdx, trainIdx)` int64 row per match between `shared/box.png` (query) and
`shared/box_in_scene.png` (train).

## Use the build under test, not ONNX Runtime

Unlike `generate_aliked_lightglue_references.py`, this script runs both models
through OpenCV DNN from the imported `cv2`, so point `PYTHONPATH` at the
`python_loader` of the OpenCV build whose `opencv_test_features` will read the
reference:

```sh
export PYTHONPATH=/path/to/opencv-build/python_loader
```

The reason is the index values. DISK's `setMaxKeypoints(1024)` keeps the top
1024 responses with an unstable `std::partial_sort`, and the saved indices point
into that order, so they cannot be canonicalized the way the ALIKED references
are — reproducing them requires the same engine that produced the scores.
`generate_disk_references.md` measures ORT's DISK scores drifting far enough
from `ENGINE_OPENCV`'s to reshuffle that list. The C++ test compares match
*sets* with a tolerance (match count within ±2, at most 3 unmatched rows on
either side) precisely because that order is not fully reproducible; `--check`
and `--check-npy` apply the same tolerance.

## Feature selection

The script mirrors `DISK_Impl::detectAndCompute` followed by the test's
`setMaxKeypoints(1024)`: drop detections with score <= 0, rescale the net-space
coordinates to the original image size, then sort by score, strongest first,
and keep the first `--max-keypoints` (default 1024) for matching. On
`box.png`/`box_in_scene.png` DISK returns 7359/7882 detections at 1024x1024, all
above the threshold, so the cap is what fixes the feature set; `--max-keypoints 0`
keeps every detection and produces a reference the C++ test cannot match, since
it asserts exactly 1024 keypoints per image.

Because the saved indices point into that score order, the features must not be
reordered by position before matching the way the ALIKED references are. The
C++ keypoint count (1024), DISK's net size (1024x1024, `DISK::create()` without
an `imageSize`), both score thresholds (0.0) and the resize (`--resize`,
defaulting to `linear-exact` as in `disk.cpp`) mirror the test and must be
revisited if it changes.

## Commands

From `testdata/dnn`:

```sh
python download_models.py disk

# Regenerate without replacing the checked-in reference.
python generate_disk_lightglue_references.py --output-dir /tmp/disk-lightglue

# Check that file AND run the C++ regression against it.
python generate_disk_lightglue_references.py --output-dir /tmp/disk-lightglue \
    --check --test-binary /path/to/opencv-build/bin/opencv_test_features

# Python/NPY comparison only; this cannot establish C++ compatibility.
python generate_disk_lightglue_references.py --check-npy
```

Inputs are `disk.onnx` and `onnx/models/disk_lightglue.onnx` under
`--models-dir` (default `testdata/dnn`), plus
`testdata/cv/shared/{box,box_in_scene}.png`. Use `--testdata` to override the
input root. Omit `--output-dir` to replace the checked-in reference.

`--check` requires `--test-binary`, writes no reference file, and exits 1 on NPY
mismatch or C++ failure. It stages a temporary testdata tree so the C++ test
reads the selected images, models and `--output-dir` reference.
`Features2d_LightGlue_DISK.Regression` must actually run and pass; a skipped or
missing test fails validation.

## Validation

Tested with Python 3.13, NumPy 2.4.0 and the local `5.x` build at `b72c45eaca`
(OpenCV 5.1.0-pre, default `ENGINE_OPENCV`), `--resize auto` resolving to
`linear-exact` from `disk.cpp`:

| Reference | `--check-npy` | C++ regression |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Committed before this script (188 matches) | FAIL (count diff 4, 3 of 188 rows in common) | FAIL (`got 184, expected 188`) |
| Generated by this script (184 matches) | PASS (identical match set) | **PASS** |

The previously committed reference was stale for this build: it shared only 3
of its 188 rows with what the build produces, which is consistent with its
indices having come from a different DISK keypoint ordering. The regenerated
file matches the C++ output exactly — the test logs no missing or extra rows,
so it passes with zero of its 3-row tolerance consumed.
